title: Financial Planning Software Pricing and Comparison
description: A pricing guide for financial planning and budgeting platforms covering Adaptive Planning, Anaplan, Budgeta, Planful, and Vena, with cost comparisons for FP&A teams.
body:
Financial planning and analysis software enables organizations to build budgets, create forecasts, model scenarios, and report on financial performance. FP&A platforms have become essential for finance teams that need to move beyond spreadsheet-based planning to more collaborative, automated, and data-driven processes.

This guide examines the pricing structures of the leading FP&A platforms. None of the platforms evaluated have published pricing verification data at the time of writing, so check each vendor's current pricing page for exact rates.

## Pricing Models in FP&A Software

FP&A platform pricing follows several distinct models. Per-user-per-month pricing is the most common approach, with costs typically higher for full users who build models and run analyses than for viewer-only users who consume reports.

Some platforms use tiered pricing based on revenue bands, with organizations paying more as their revenue grows. This model aligns platform cost with organizational value but creates pricing uncertainty for high-growth companies.

Enterprise FP&A platforms frequently use custom pricing based on entity count, data volume, and selected modules. These contracts typically include implementation services and dedicated support.

Implementation costs for FP&A platforms are significant. Financial planning software requires data integration, model configuration, and team training that typically add thirty to fifty percent to first-year costs. Budget for professional services when evaluating total cost.

Check each vendor's current pricing page for exact rates and implementation cost estimates.

## Adaptive Planning

Adaptive Planning serves mid-market and enterprise organizations with a focus on financial modeling, budgeting, and reporting. Its pricing is structured around plan tiers that scale with feature requirements and user count.

Adaptive Planning's core capabilities include driver-based budgeting, multi-dimensional modeling, what-if scenario analysis, and automated reporting. The platform integrates with major ERP and accounting systems.

Adaptive Planning's pricing varies based on the number of model builders versus report consumers. Organizations with large finance teams that need many full-user licenses face higher costs than those where few model builders serve many report consumers.

Check Adaptive Planning's current pricing page for exact rates, as Workday (Adaptive Planning's parent company) quotes custom pricing.

## Anaplan

Anaplan serves large enterprises with complex planning needs that span finance, sales, supply chain, and workforce planning. Anaplan's hyperblock technology enables multi-dimensional modeling that traditional OLAP-based platforms cannot match.

Anaplan's pricing is custom-quoted based on user count, workspace capacity, and selected applications. The platform's enterprise focus means minimum annual commitments are significant.

Anaplan's total cost should include workspace subscription, user licenses for model builders and viewers, and implementation partner fees. Typical enterprise deployments involve substantial professional services for model development and integration.

Check Anaplan's current pricing page for exact rates, as pricing is customized for each deployment.

## Planful

Planful serves mid-market organizations with a focus on financial close management, budgeting, and reporting. Its pricing is typically per-user-per-month with tiered feature availability.

Planful's strengths include automated financial consolidation, intercompany elimination, and compliance reporting. The platform also provides budgeting, forecasting, and scenario modeling capabilities that serve core FP&A needs.

Planful's pricing is competitive for mid-market organizations that need financial close and planning capabilities without the enterprise complexity of Anaplan or Adaptive Planning.

Check Planful's current pricing page for exact rates.

## Vena

Vena combines Excel-based modeling with cloud-based collaboration, workflow automation, and reporting. This approach allows finance teams to build models in Excel while benefiting from centralized data management and process automation.

Vena's pricing is based on user count and selected feature modules. The Excel-centric approach reduces the learning curve for finance teams but requires Excel expertise for model development.

Vena's pricing typically includes model development services, as the platform's value depends on the quality of the Excel-based planning models.

Check Vena's current pricing page for exact rates.

## Selection Guidance

The right FP&A platform depends on organizational complexity, model sophistication, and finance team expertise. Organizations with straightforward planning needs and limited finance headcount benefit from spreadsheet-integrated platforms like Vena. Mid-market companies should evaluate Planful for its balance of capability and cost. Enterprises with complex multi-dimensional planning needs require Adaptive Planning or Anaplan.
